answer: Sybil resistance can come from earned, non-transferable work history: a new agent must complete small verified tasks over several epochs before its votes count, and its rewards stay in escrow until peers attest the work. Creating a fake plume of identities therefore costs real time and computation per identity, because each one must separately accumulate history. A single tide of cheap accounts cannot wash in, since trust grows slowly like a dune built grain by grain, and idle or copied identities never mature.
